cases.name: Elizabeth 'Tsontso' Moselakgomo
cases.linkStatus: Under task team investigation. No one has been charged with her murder. Three men face theft, money-laundering and related charges over her smartwatch (not murder).
cases.statusShort: under task team investigation; no murder charge; 3 men charged over her smartwatch

lastSeen.place: Left home for an afternoon/evening run (Kempton Park area; her home suburb is reported inconsistently, so it is not mapped)

found.place: Behind a hotel in Rhodesfield, Kempton Park (York Street, per Daily Maverick)
found.placeNote: Found on the evening/night of Saturday 12 September.

cases.circumstances: A runner who did not return from her run; her eight-year-old daughter raised the alarm. Found badly bruised and partially clothed. Her family identified her at the Germiston mortuary on 14 September. She was buried in Mpumalanga around 19-20 September. Her disappearance drew wide public attention.
cases.legal: On the morning of 12 October, national police spokesperson Brigadier Athlenda Mathe confirmed that a suspect had been arrested after being found in possession of an item belonging to Moselakgomo, and said no murder charge had been brought. That afternoon three men appeared in the Kempton Park Magistrates' Court over her Garmin smartwatch (NPA). They face charges of theft and money laundering, with alternative charges of possessing or receiving stolen property; one, who ran a second-hand goods shop in Kempton Park, also faces charges under the Second-Hand Goods Act. The State alleges the watch was bought for R900 from an unidentified person less than 24 hours after she was last seen, then sold on and advertised on social media. A fourth person who bought the watch was not charged because of insufficient evidence (NPA). Two of the men were granted bail of R10,000 each; the State did not oppose it (Sowetan). The third remains in custody: his bail application was postponed to 19 October and the court ordered that his immigration status be verified. None of the three is charged with her murder, and police say the murder investigation continues. The accused are presumed innocent and are not named here.

Where she was found: Daily Maverick says behind a hotel on York Street, Rhodesfield; EWN (13 Oct) says along the R21 in Kempton Park; Sowetan says in bushes in Kempton Park.

cases.name: Jabulile Ntimba
cases.linkStatus: Arrest made: two women charged. Police cite a possible relationship ('love triangle') motive and have not linked this case to the others.
cases.statusShort: arrest made - two women charged (separate motive per police)

found.place: Open area on Lama Street, Villa Liza, Dawn Park (Boksburg)

cases.circumstances: Found partially clothed with a fatal throat injury (as reported).
cases.legal: Three people were arrested over the weekend of 19-20 September by the Gauteng Murder and Robbery Unit. A man was released: prosecutors declined to enrol charges, though police said he remains under investigation. Two women were charged with premeditated murder and defeating the ends of justice. They appeared in the Boksburg Magistrates' Court on 21 September and were remanded in custody. Their bail proceedings began on 1 October, when the first accused alleged in an affidavit that police had tortured her into confessing and said she did not kill Ntimba. The court has not tested these allegations. The matter was postponed to 12 October. No report describing the 12 October hearing was found; Daily Maverick reported on 13 October that both remain in custody, and SABC reported on 19 October that the two accused were expected back in the Boksburg Magistrates' Court that morning for the continuation of their bail applications. SABC lists the charges as premeditated murder, possession of a dangerous weapon, and defeating or obstructing the course of justice. As of the morning of 19 October, no outcome had been reported. They are presumed innocent and are not named on this site.

cases.circumstances: Found with serious head injuries; stones were found nearby and the Gauteng commissioner said she may have been stoned (as reported). Residents reported hearing screams at about 23:00 on Friday. Her friend identified her by her clothes. She leaves five children; her family planned a burial in Nongoma, KwaZulu-Natal. Age reported as 49 (EWN, The Citizen).
cases.legal: A 36-year-old man was traced to a village in Limpopo and arrested (in Tzaneen / Mohlabaneng Village, according to reports). He appeared in the Tembisa Magistrates' Court on 29 September, charged with murder. On 6 October the formal bail application did not proceed: the defence asked for more time to consult, and the matter was postponed to 19 October. The State said it was ready to proceed and will oppose bail. He remains in custody (Daily Maverick, 13 October, also reports he remains in custody until the 19 October appearance). As of the morning of 19 October, no outcome had been reported. He is presumed innocent and is not named on this site.
